## Web research: crypto.randomBytes for password reset tokens

Question: "Write Given-When-Then acceptance criteria for our password reset token, based on what https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html says about crypto.randomBytes."

### Facts
1. crypto.randomBytes produces cryptographically strong pseudorandom data. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "Generates cryptographically strong pseudorandom data."
2. The size argument is the number of bytes to generate. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "The size argument is a number indicating the number of bytes to generate."
3. The size has an upper limit. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "The size must not be larger than 2**31 - 1."
4. If you pass a callback, the bytes are generated asynchronously and the callback gets an error and a buffer. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "If a callback function is provided, the bytes are generated asynchronously and the callback function is invoked with two arguments: err and buf."
5. In callback mode, a failure is reported through err. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "If an error occurs, err will be an Error object; otherwise it is null."
6. Without a callback, generation is synchronous and returns a Buffer. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "If the callback function is not provided, the random bytes are generated synchronously and returned as a Buffer."
7. In synchronous mode, a failure throws an error. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "An error will be thrown if there is a problem generating the bytes."
8. The method waits until enough entropy is available. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "The crypto.randomBytes() method will not complete until there is sufficient entropy available."
9. The wait is normally short. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "This should normally never take longer than a few milliseconds."
10. Longer blocking can happen right after boot. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "The only time when generating the random bytes may conceivably block for a longer period of time is right after boot..."
11. The API uses libuv's threadpool, which can hurt performance. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "This API uses libuv's threadpool, which can have surprising and negative performance implications for some applications..."
12. The docs advise splitting large requests made while serving a client. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html "To minimize threadpool task length variation, partition large randomBytes requests when doing so as part of fulfilling a client request."

### Inferences
- Reset tokens should be built from crypto.randomBytes output, since it is documented as cryptographically strong (from facts 1, 2).
- The spec should say how a failed generation is handled. No token should be issued when err is set or an error is thrown (from facts 5, 7).
- In the reset-request path, the asynchronous form avoids blocking the event loop. Token sizes are small, so splitting requests is not needed (from facts 4, 6, 11, 12).
- The spec should allow for a slower first reset request right after a server boots (from facts 8, 9, 10).
